I’ll read the handoff and repository guidance, then continue the research from the next steps in the note.

The handoff identifies two issues to test: the frequency cutoff grows rapidly with the window, and the current bound discards positive energy before projecting onto the constrained source space. I’m replaying the length-one certificate and auditing the dilation formulas in parallel. The next calculation will stay at \(L=6/5\), where primes 2 and 3 are active.

The length-one replay passed and reproduced the saved matrix hash. The analytic audit also found a useful simplification: relative compactness extends to every fixed finite prime set using the bounded correction and compact resolvent of the source operator. This avoids needing a separate Hilbert–Schmidt proof for the two-prime correction kernel, though quantitative bounds are still needed.

At \(L=6/5\), the floating pilot shows that the original capped bound fails because it discards positive energy. Retaining signed contributions gives a small positive margin. I’ve recorded the cost and error budget and am now testing it with outward arithmetic, including every omitted source mode.

The new certificate passed. It proves \(Q[F]\ge 3/2000\,\|F\|_2^2\) for the full prepared mean-zero source class at \(L=6/5\), including both parities and complex sources. With the recalculated two-prime correction bound, this gives \(Q[F]\ge(3/6916003)B[F]\). A separate 256-bit replay is underway; the all-window estimate remains open.

The 256-bit replay also passed, and its scalar enclosures agree with the 192-bit run. I’m finishing the research record: the signed comparison, the discarded-energy diagnosis, and the finite-set compactness argument. The original certificate and manuscript remain unchanged.

Completed the bounded extension to \(L=6/5\). For the original prepared mean-zero source class, with fixed prime set \(\{2,3\}\), the new certificate proves
\[
Q[F]\ge \frac{3}{2000}\|F\|_2^2,
\qquad
Q[F]\ge \frac{3}{6916003}B_{\{2,3\}}[F].
\]

It passed at 192 and 256 bits, including all omitted source modes. Retaining signed frequency contributions repaired the earlier bound’s loss of positive energy.

The analytic work also establishes relative compactness for every fixed finite prime set without requiring a Hilbert–Schmidt correction kernel. Quantitative control along an **unbounded sequence of windows** remains open.

Saved the [research outcome](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/notes/ALL_WINDOW_EXTENSION_OUTCOME_20261003.md), [certificate package and audits](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/numerics/all_window_extension_20261003/README.md), and [next-session handoff](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/notes/NEXT_SESSION_SIGNED_COMPARISON_HANDOFF_20261003.md).

The original certificate and manuscript are unchanged. Reviews were internal, within the same model family.
Please continue with pursuing the all-window mechanism

I’ll build on the signed certificate and finite-set compactness result, focusing on an estimate that could control arbitrarily large windows. I’ll first examine the spectral tails and mixed terms, alongside the signed prime-discrepancy approach.

The earlier repository work already contains several of the generic finite-dimensional reductions, so those alone won’t advance this step. Two sharper questions are emerging: how to make the relative spectral split effective, and how much long-range prime cancellation is forced by positivity between translated sources. The centered main term also needs care: its negative low-frequency directions persist as the window grows.

There is now a precise obstruction to separating the tail estimates: removing any finite number of source directions leaves the arithmetic operator’s exponential-size norm intact. Combining that norm with a separate scalar archimedean bound forces doubly exponential rank.

A bounded probe check illustrates the cancellation this loses. At separation 12, the absolute prime sum is about 90.36, while the signed sum has magnitude about 0.7774. The corresponding two-source Gram matrix passes an outward check. This tests the cancellation mechanism, not positivity on the full larger window.

The audits passed. The work now narrows the viable route: the estimate must keep arithmetic alignment tied to source energy. Bare \(L^2\) bounds on the centered discrepancy, fixed-rank repairs of the centered main term, and separate scalar tail bounds have proved limitations.

I’ve also derived a finite-column certificate that retains the mixed terms and gives a complete residual bound. It makes the required calculation precise, but the available constants are too pessimistic to justify a large run.

Continued the analytic program. The all-window inequality remains open, but three concrete advances are recorded:

- **Effective relative tails:** an approximation retaining mixed terms has rank at most \(2n\) and error at most \(k/b_{n+1}\). I also derived a certificate using full equation residuals.
- **A rigorous limitation:** removing any finite source head leaves the arithmetic norm unchanged. Separately bounding arithmetic and archimedean tails therefore forces doubly exponential rank. The centered reference also requires a growing negative-frequency block.
- **Validated cancellation tests:** five translated-source Gram matrices passed at 192 and 256 bits. At separation 12, the absolute prime sum is about \(90.36\), while the signed sum has magnitude \(0.7774\). These are two-source checks, not full-window certificates.

The remaining estimate must control **signed arithmetic together with source energy**, including mixed terms, along unbounded windows.

Saved the [research outcome](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/notes/ALL_WINDOW_MECHANISM_OUTCOME_20261003.md), [internal audit](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/reviews/ALL_WINDOW_MECHANISM_FINAL_REVIEW_20261003.md), and [reproducible calculations](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations/sonin-critical-boundary/numerics/all_window_mechanism_20261003/README.md). Earlier certificates and the manuscript are unchanged.
